segments: Let's see how to compute Kimi Delta Attention in chunks. We will reorganize the recurrence without changing its result.
Each token decays the memory, predicts its value, writes a correction, and then reads the updated memory with its query.
The next prediction needs the previous token's updated state. Putting boundaries around this same loop does not make it parallel.
We will follow three tokens, two key channels, and one value feature. For this example, queries equal keys and the incoming memory is one, one.
A new correction is written after its own token's decay. Only the later gates can shrink that correction.
Add log retentions instead of multiplying retentions. A difference of prefix sums gives the interval.
Incoming memory is different. It existed before the chunk, so its decay includes every gate through the current token.
A key reads an earlier correction through a dot product. Aligned keys interact strongly. Orthogonal keys do not.
First decay the writer's key, channel by channel. Then take the dot product and scale it by the writer's beta.
In this example the coefficient is point one five. Multiplying it by the first error adds point one eight to the second prediction.
Errors depend only on earlier writes. The matrix is strictly lower triangular, excluding future and current writes.
The base error uses only decayed incoming memory. Subtract contributions from earlier corrections to get the actual error.
Move the earlier errors to the left. This gives a triangular system, with one row per token.
Incoming memory gives the predictions shown here. Subtract them from the target values to get the right hand side, capital B.
The first error is one point two.
Correct the second prediction. Error one becomes one point zero zero four.
Subtract both earlier corrections. Error two is about one point seven seven four.
A compiled triangular solver handles the dependencies and batches heads and value features. No matrix inverse is needed.
Now read the outputs: incoming memory plus the error contributions. This time, use query vectors in the coefficient matrix.
Outputs include the diagonal: each query reads its own write. The error matrix excludes it.
Decay the incoming state and add all surviving corrections to get the outgoing memory. The outputs and state match the token loop exactly.
The layer's keys, queries, gates, and write strengths are already known. We can prepare local coefficients for many chunks and heads together.
Carry state between chunks. Inside each chunk, matrix operations replace the Python token loop.
Only a fixed size memory state moves between chunks. Local token interactions have chunk size squared entries, rather than sequence length squared.
This triangular system is practical for learning. The paper's fused GPU kernels require more engineering.
Block operations do not guarantee speed. Stability, temporary memory, and the backend still matter.
Keep causal dependencies, but collect them into block equations. Same result, different computation.
